title: Larry on patrol with a captured prisoner
description: Larry, in duck-hunter camouflage, crouches low in dense jungle looking back over his shoulder into the lens. Close behind him crouches a man who, in Larry's account, was a prisoner: found in a hut by Sgt. Lowry and brought out tied up. "No idea what he did." The picture, his son relayed, was taken by Captain Kennedy with his Nikon F, and the blurred face further back is one of the strikers, the camp's strike-force irregulars.
researchNotes: Relayed by Larry's son from Larry's dictation (2026-08-15 session; archived as data/recollections/giscus-vn-0023-c18035445.json, -c18035515.json, and -c18035521.json). Unusual provenance, on his son's report: a photograph of Captain Kennedy's print (developed in Hawaii), which would explain any generational quality loss and would put Kennedy with Larry that day; because it rests on a paraphrase, it is not used to strengthen the tentative VN-0006 identification. Larry's own camera, his son relayed, was a Canon Dial 35, bought at the Qui Nhơn PX (VN-0016 comment). The first of the three 2026-08-15 records is held from the site (2026-09-14) because it labels the prisoner, and the guide asks that no label be offered to him. 2026-09-12 (giscus-vn-0023-c18415971.json, transcribed): a fuller account in his own words. The two accounts differ on who the prisoner was; that comparison is kept out of this record (research/photos/held-from-records-2026-09-14.md; ledger #17, issue #97). New in the 2026-09-12 account: Sgt. Lowry found the man in a hut, so Lowry was on this patrol or with it (data/people/sgt-lowry.json, issue #12), though Larry does not say Lowry is in the frame and he is not linked; the girlfriend sent away; and the hand-off in two stages, to the ARVN and then to the CIA. Location: 'to the left of Nui Ba Den' — a patrol in the country beside the mountain, not on it, so no place is set; the nui-ba-den record is the mountain and its camp.
